comments.text:
I really loved how this game took place in the Arklay Mountains and its surrounding areas. I liked how they revealed that there was another city nearby that was basically another Raccoon City. I love how timeless Wrenwood feels with the fashion of the people, it still having pay phones, and many of the cars you see are old models.

1:41:14 However, I didn't love how the game pretends Leon doesn't exist because the camera isn't pointed at him. When he is in frame again, you hear him shout "Hey!" and go for his gun, but he's too late to do anything to stop her from being killed. 

But he still had plenty of time to act before that. I don't know why the scene insisted on lingering on the zombie for so long. Her death should have been a sudden thing that was completely unavoidable. The game pretends that's the case, but it isn't.

Maybe have some zombies start rustling around in the corridor, so Leon leaves the nurse in the examination room to deal with it. Only to rush in after hearing her screaming only to see her getting killed the moment you open the door.

8:17:28 What is it with this director in having snappy black characters who died basically immediately? At least this guy was substantially smarter than the cop from Resident Evil 7.

8:18:31 I don't think that's what happened here. I think it's just a simple mistake in timing. I think the frame was supposed to break when he sweeps the butt of the gun back and forth. They just had it break a bit too early.

comments.text: Grace is a desk worker, not a field agent. She was only sent to investigate a crime scene. There was no reason to think there would be fighting or they would have sent backup with her. Why send her without backup? Because it was not needed for the task she was given. And she has likely never killed anyone before. She is not Jill or Claire. Her not shooting attackers immediately is a natural reaction when you are scared. Especially for someone who is not an in control badass like Leon.
